authoredPrompt: This figure is a line graph of four straight lines tracing free energy against temperature for the four sign combinations of enthalpy and entropy change. The vertical axis is labeled Free energy and the horizontal axis Increasing temperature (K); the only numeral shown is 0 on the vertical axis. A gray dashed line at that zero splits the field into a pink upper half labeled Nonspontaneous, with delta G greater than 0 printed beside the axis, and a green lower half labeled Spontaneous, with delta G less than 0. All four lines start at the left edge. A red line begins high in the pink field and climbs to the upper right, labeled delta H greater than 0, delta S less than 0, while a green line begins in the green field and falls to the lower right, labeled delta H less than 0, delta S greater than 0. Two yellow lines lie between them and both cross the dashed zero line: one starts in the pink field and slopes downward, labeled delta H greater than 0, delta S greater than 0, the other starts in the green field and slopes upward, labeled delta H less than 0, delta S less than 0. Starting half and slope sign together encode the two arithmetic signs, so only the yellow pair changes shading as temperature rises, each at its own x-intercept. The plot motivates why a process whose enthalpy and entropy changes share a sign reverses spontaneity at the temperature where free energy is zero.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for temperature: learner drags a vertical temperature cursor across the plot, and each line's current delta G point lights in the spontaneous or nonspontaneous region, showing how temperature changes spontaneity through delta G = delta H - T delta S.
- Toggle between sign combinations: learner selects one delta H, delta S pair at a time, and the chosen line is isolated while its intercept and slope are emphasized, making clear that delta H sets the starting side and delta S sets how delta G changes with temperature.
authoredContext:
Such a plot is shown in the figure. A process whose enthalpy and entropy changes are of the same arithmetic sign will exhibit a temperature-dependent spontaneity as depicted by the two yellow lines in the plot. Each line crosses from one spontaneity domain (positive or negative ΔG) to the other at a temperature that is characteristic of the process in question. This temperature is represented by the x-intercept of the line, that is, the value of T for which ΔG is zero:

So, saying a process is spontaneous at “high” or “low” temperatures means the temperature is above or below, respectively, that temperature at which ΔG for the process is zero. As noted earlier, the condition of ΔG = 0 describes a system at equilibrium.

These plots show the variation in ΔG with temperature for the four possible combinations of arithmetic sign for ΔH and ΔS.

A graph is shown where the y-axis is labeled, “Free energy,” and the x-axis is labeled, “Increasing temperature (K).” The value of zero is written midway up the y-axis with the label, “delta G greater than 0,” written above this line and, “delta G less than 0,” written below it. The bottom half of the graph is labeled on the right as, “Spontaneous,” and the top half is labeled on the right as, “Nonspontaneous.” A green line labeled, “delta H less than 0, delta S greater than 0,” extends from a quarter of the way up the y-axis to the bottom right of the graph. A yellow line labeled, “delta H less than 0, delta S less than 0,” extends from a quarter of the way up the y-axis to the middle right of the graph. A second yellow line labeled, “delta H greater than 0, delta S greater than 0,” extends from three quarters of the way up the y-axis to the middle right of the graph. A red line labeled, “delta H greater than 0, delta S less than 0,” extends from three quarters of the way up the y-axis to the top right of the graph.

discrepancies: The two yellow same-sign lines meet and cross the zero boundary much farther left and higher than in the source, where their transition point is near the dashed zero line on the right half of the plot.
A temperature cursor and white-outlined colored endpoint markers are visible in the default state, but the source figure has only plain colored lines with no markers or cursor.
Several line labels are not placed as faithfully as the source: the yellow/green lower labels sit lower and the upper labels are less centered along their corresponding sloped lines.
The region text is close but not identical in placement; the generated 'Nonspontaneous' label is pushed very near the right edge compared with the more comfortably inset source label.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is clearly recognizable and conceptually useful, but the yellow transition geometry is noticeably shifted and the default interactive cursor/markers prevent it from being a clean static replacement.
action_items: Adjust the yellow line slopes/intercepts so their zero crossing and mutual intersection occur near the dashed ΔG = 0 line on the right half of the plot, matching the source schematic.
Hide the temperature cursor and circular markers in the default step, or make them appear only after the user moves the slider or enables a focus mode.
Reposition the sloped sign-pair labels to sit more centrally on their corresponding lines and keep the lower labels farther from the bottom border.
Move the 'Nonspontaneous' label slightly left so it has the same inset spacing as the source.
